name: Civiloris
hero:
Property is complex.
Your counsel should be clear.
intro: A focused legal practice at the intersection of Indian real estate, development and regulation.
address: Floor 3, Barakhamba Road, Connaught Place, New Delhi, Delhi 110001, India

leadership.name: Aditi Malhotra
leadership.role: Managing Partner | Real Estate, Investment & Development
leadership.summary: Aditi advises on the legal and commercial dimensions of real estate acquisitions, development arrangements and property investments. Her practice integrates transaction structuring, regulatory assessment and contractual risk allocation.
leadership.bio: Aditi's professional interests centre on the relationship between land, capital and development. She approaches real estate transactions as decisions that establish the financial, legal and institutional foundations of a development. Her career evolved from property documentation and transaction execution towards complex acquisitions, development agreements and commercial arrangements. In 2018, she co-founded Civiloris to integrate legal diligence, development feasibility and commercial decision-making. As managing partner, she oversees the firm's strategic direction and coordinates multidisciplinary property matters, emphasising early risk identification and alignment between contractual obligations and commercial objectives. She also holds an MBA from the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB) and a PhD in Economics from the University of Pennsylvania (UPenn).
education: B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) — National Law University, Jodhpur
Master of Business Administration (MBA) — Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB)
Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Economics — University of Pennsylvania (UPenn)
leadership.sectors: Residential, commercial, mixed-use and industrial property; land development.
research: Real estate investment frameworks, institutional capital, joint-development risk allocation and the relationship between regulation and investment

leadership.name: Dhruv Sinha
leadership.summary: Dhruv specialises in the legal foundations of property ownership, examining historical transfers, land records, encumbrances and contractual arrangements to establish transaction risks.
leadership.bio: Dhruv's practice is built around a fundamental question: what rights does a property owner hold, and what can legally be transferred or developed? His interests extend beyond individual title documents to the historical, administrative and contractual relationships that determine a property's status. His career developed across title investigation, acquisition diligence, commercial property documentation and lease arrangements. As a co-founder of Civiloris, he leads the land and title practice, identifying ownership discrepancies, evaluating documentary evidence and translating diligence findings into contractual safeguards. He works with the transaction and planning teams where ownership intersects with development rights, access and regulatory restrictions.
education: B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) — Gujarat National Law University, Gandhinagar

career.title: Commercial property transactions and contractual structuring

leadership.sectors: Land parcels, commercial offices, industrial estates, residential developments and logistics facilities.
research: Land administration, digitisation of property records, ownership transparency, title assurance and legal certainty

leadership.name: Kavya Rotta
leadership.summary: Kavya advises on regulatory frameworks governing land use, property development and urban transformation, examining how planning legislation and institutional requirements influence project feasibility.
leadership.bio: Kavya works at the intersection of law, urban planning and development policy. Her career began with land-use legislation, statutory research and interpretation, later expanding into development permissions and planning-policy changes. At Civiloris, she leads planning and regulatory advisory, treating regulatory assessment as an integral component of investment and development decisions. Her work connects statutory requirements with site characteristics, including permitted uses, development potential, physical constraints and approval requirements. She collaborates with the planning and transaction teams to identify regulatory risks before major commitments are made.
education: B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) — NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad
leadership.sectors: Urban redevelopment, residential projects, mixed-use projects, industrial development and large-scale land development.
research: Urban governance, planning-law reform, development rights, regulatory uncertainty and urban growth institutions

leadership.name: Raghav Menon
leadership.summary: Raghav focuses on the prevention, management and resolution of disputes arising from property transactions, development agreements and commercial relationships.
leadership.bio: Raghav's approach begins with understanding the circumstances behind a dispute: what was agreed, what changed and which records support each position. His career developed across contractual claims, commercial disputes and property-related disagreements. At Civiloris, he leads dispute assessment and resolution strategy, working with the transaction and regulatory teams to understand the legal and commercial implications of each matter. He emphasises evidence-based assessment, proportionate intervention and the evaluation of negotiated outcomes alongside formal dispute resolution mechanisms.
education: B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) — Hidayatullah National Law University, Raipur
leadership.sectors: Property development, construction, commercial leasing, joint development ventures and land transactions.
research: Alternative dispute resolution, contractual governance, construction risk allocation and the economics of property disputes

leadership.name: Meera Iyer
leadership.summary: Meera specialises in the spatial, institutional and economic dimensions of urban development, connecting land-use strategies and development potential with real estate investment requirements.
leadership.bio: Meera approaches land as part of a wider urban system. Its development potential depends not only on legal status and physical characteristics, but also on infrastructure availability, accessibility, surrounding development and long-term urban change. Her career developed from spatial analysis and land development towards development feasibility, infrastructure assessment and strategic planning. At Civiloris, she leads urban planning and development advisory, working with Kavya on regulatory constraints and Aditi on the development implications of acquisitions. Her contribution is to establish what a site can realistically accommodate and which planning considerations should influence development decisions.
education: Bachelor of Planning (B.Plan.) — School of Planning and Architecture, New Delhi
Master of Planning (Urban Planning) — School of Planning and Architecture, New Delhi

career.title: Spatial planning and urban development analysis
Strategic planning and real estate development advisory
Director, Urban Planning & Development Advisory, Civiloris

leadership.sectors: Urban redevelopment, residential communities, mixed-use development, industrial townships and urban infrastructure.
research: Urban economics, land-value capture, infrastructure-led development, spatial decision-making and computational urban planning

leadership.name: Anuradha Desai
leadership.role: Director | Real Estate Finance & Investment Advisory
leadership.summary: Anuradha specialises in the financial dimensions of real estate development, including investment appraisal, project feasibility, capital structuring and financial risk assessment.
leadership.bio: Anuradha's interests centre on how capital influences the development of land and property. A project may be legally permissible and technically feasible while remaining financially unviable. Her approach examines acquisition costs, financing arrangements, development expenditure, market demand and expected returns. Her career developed across financial analysis, investment evaluation, real estate economics and development finance. At Civiloris, she leads financial advisory, working with legal, planning and development teams to evaluate the financial implications of acquisition conditions, regulatory uncertainty and project delivery. She emphasises transparent assumptions, scenario analysis and the distinction between projected returns and associated risks.
education: B.Com. (Hons.) — Shri Ram College of Commerce, University of Delhi
Master of Business Administration (MBA) — Faculty of Management Studies, University of Delhi

career.title: Real estate investment and project feasibility
Director, Real Estate Finance & Investment Advisory, Civiloris

leadership.sectors: Commercial real estate, residential developments, industrial property, mixed-use developments and income-generating assets.
research: Real estate capital markets, infrastructure financing, institutional investment, REITs and emerging financial technologies

leadership.name: Vikram Bhatia
leadership.summary: Vikram specialises in construction management, development delivery and project risk, examining the technical, contractual and operational factors that influence project completion.
leadership.bio: Vikram's approach is grounded in the distinction between planning a development and delivering it. Construction costs, procurement, scheduling, design changes and stakeholder coordination influence financial performance and contractual obligations. His career developed from civil engineering and construction management towards project controls, procurement strategies and development risk. At Civiloris, he leads construction and development risk advisory, collaborating with Raghav on construction disputes, Anuradha on development expenditure and Meera on implementation. His work focuses on identifying delivery risks before they become contractual, financial or operational problems.
education: B.Tech. in Civil Engineering — Indian Institute of Technology Delhi
M.Tech. in Construction Engineering and Management — Indian Institute of Technology Delhi
leadership.sectors: Commercial buildings, residential developments, industrial facilities, mixed-use projects and infrastructure construction.
research: Construction economics, digital project delivery, building information modelling, procurement innovation and infrastructure lifecycle risk

leadership.name: Naina Kapoor
leadership.summary: Naina undertakes legislative research, regulatory analysis and policy monitoring to support Civiloris's property, planning and dispute advisory practices.
leadership.bio: Naina is interested in how legislation, government policy and judicial interpretation influence real estate development. Her work examines statutory provisions, administrative notifications and regulatory documents to identify implications for individual matters. After developing a foundation in legal research and litigation support, she joined Civiloris in 2023. She contributes to regulatory assessments, comparative legislative analysis and internal knowledge resources, emphasising source verification, legislative context and clear communication of complex requirements.
education: B.B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) — Symbiosis Law School, Pune
leadership.sectors: Urban development regulation, real estate policy, property administration and development approvals.
research: Regulatory transparency, digital legal research, comparative planning legislation and legal knowledge systems

leadership.name: Armaan Sharoon
leadership.summary: Armaan supports commercial property transactions, lease negotiations and acquisition documentation, focusing on contractual clarity and transaction execution.
leadership.bio: Armaan is interested in how commercial agreements translate investment intentions into enforceable rights and responsibilities. His work concentrates on contractual conditions, lease obligations, documentation requirements and completion procedures. After developing a foundation in commercial leasing and transaction support, he joined Civiloris in 2024. Working alongside senior transaction professionals, he contributes to document preparation, agreement review and coordination of outstanding contractual requirements. His approach emphasises drafting precision and the commercial implications of individual provisions.
education: B.A. LL.B. (Hons.) — Institute of Law, Nirma University, Ahmedabad
leadership.sectors: Commercial offices, retail property, industrial facilities, logistics and warehousing.
research: Commercial lease structures, contractual automation, transaction efficiency and real estate legal technology

services.title: Real Estate Transactions
services.heading: Clarity in the transaction.
services.description: Property acquisitions, disposals and leases bring legal rights, documentation and commercial objectives together. Civiloris examines those elements in the context of the transaction.

services.title: Development & Joint Ventures
services.heading: A shared development objective.
services.description: Development arrangements depend on a clear understanding of land rights, contributions, responsibilities and the commercial expectations of the parties.

services.title: Regulatory & RERA Matters
services.heading: The regulatory context of development.
services.description: Real estate development engages statutory obligations, administrative processes and relationships between promoters and purchasers. The applicable framework depends on the project and jurisdiction.

services.title: Land Use & Planning Law
services.heading: Law in the context of place.
services.description: The legal status of land and its development potential are shaped by planning designations, statutory controls and the characteristics of the site.

services.title: Title & Property Due Diligence
services.heading: Understanding the rights in land.
services.description: A property decision requires an understanding of the rights that can be transferred, the interests affecting them and the reliability of the underlying records.

services.title: Property Disputes & Resolution
services.heading: The facts behind a disagreement.
services.description: Property disputes often arise from differing interpretations of rights, contracts, obligations or the circumstances of development and occupation.
